newsitem.title: USA: Schawk agrees to sell plastics group.
newsitem.headline: Schawk agrees to sell plastics group.

text.p: Schawk Inc said Thursday it entered into a definitive agreement to sell its plastics group to ESCO Electronics Corp for about $92.0 million in cash plus working capital adjustments.
The company said it will take a charge from the sale of its discontinued plastics group of $33.0 million or $1.65 a share, which includes estimated tax liabilities.
The transaction is expected to be accretive based on projected 1997 net income, it added.

"The divestiture of our plastics group is consistent with the strategy we articulated at our 1996 annual stockholders meeting, which is to sharpen our focus on our core imaging products and services businesses," David Schawk, chief executive officer, said in a statement.
He added the transaction also will allow Schawk to reduce debt and strengthen its balance sheet, grow its imaging and technology business through selective acquisitions and enhance shareholder value.
In a separate statement, ESCO said the acquired business will operate as a subsidiary known as Filtertek Inc.

ESCO said Filtertek will be added to its Filtration/Fluid Flow business, which will then account for about one-third of the company's total sales volume and substantially increase its presence in this growing market.

"The acquisition of Filtertek will not only strengthen our market position in Filtration/Fluid Flow, but will also materially change our overall business mix," Dennis Moore, ESCO chairman, said in a statement. "Increasing the company's commercial business base has been an important element to our strategy for several years."
With the acquisition of Filtertek, ESCO said its commercial sales will exceed defense sales on an annualized basis for the first time in its history.
The transaction is expected to close within 60 days.
